verses.1: A wise child avoids causing his father to get angry.
verses.2: From the fruit of one’s mouth, one may eat good things and live a life of joy.
verses.3: He seals his lips, protecting his soul.
verses.4: His soul is weighed down and burdened; his spirit is filled with sorrow.
verses.5: False words are hated by the righteous, while the wicked bring harm and destruction.
verses.6: Justice will create a path for salvation, while wickedness will be erased along with one’s sins.
verses.7: Some things are difficult to do, but not everything is impossible. And there are many things that can be done.
verses.8: The “Cohen of the Soul” was made by someone who didn’t listen to any complaints.
verses.9: The righteous will rejoice, but the wicked will be destroyed.
verses.10: Only by faith can one receive guidance and wise counsel.
verses.11: He is light in weight and strong in strength, with the help of Yarbeh.
verses.12: It begins with a heart disease, and then there’s also the problem of living trees.
verses.13: In that case, he will be punished for his actions. He will fear the commandment.
verses.14: The wisdom of the sage brings life from the depths of death.
verses.15: A good mind brings grace and a way to act righteously.
verses.16: Every city will be built with wisdom, and the foolish will be destroyed.
verses.17: The wicked king will fall into evil ways, and the truthful people will be freed from their suffering.
verses.18: Reish and Kalo’n are responsible for delivering and storing the treasures.
verses.19: Anger will become a burden on the soul, and it will cause suffering like that of the foolish.
verses.20: The wise go astray, while the foolish are led astray.
verses.21: Sinners will be pursued by evil, but the righteous will receive good in return.
verses.22: Good will be passed down to sons, and hope will be given to the righteous.
verses.23: Many people have eaten too much, and some have died without being judged.
verses.24: He who dislikes his own power, and loves those who are under his control.
verses.25: The righteous eat to satisfy their souls, while the wicked have nothing to eat.
